title: bug: an empty daemon.lock (acquireLock's O_EXCL create-to-write window) is judged 'malformed lock' and replaced, so two simultaneous starts can both take the lock
description: acquireLock (packages/moe-daemon/src/index.ts) creates daemon.lock with O_EXCL and writes its JSON in a second syscall. A contender that reads the still-empty file in between gets staleLockReason 'malformed lock', unlinks it and wins its retry, so on POSIX both processes start a daemon over one .moe/. Scratch-probe repro: an empty lock gives staleLockReason='malformed lock' and the contender's acquireLock=true. This is pre-existing and the window is narrow. task-25ba449a's plan forbids lock-policy changes, so it is filed here. One fix is to treat a young empty lock as live, for example by checking mtime against a short grace period.

implementationPlan.description:
FIX (GREEN) in packages/moe-daemon/src/index.ts. Only the type and three functions change.

- `LockInfo` gains optional `empty?: boolean`.
- `readLockInfo`:
  - The empty-content branch (`if (!raw) return null;`) instead returns `{ pid: null, projectPath: null, createdAtMs: stat.mtimeMs, empty: true }`, from the same statSync/readFileSync snapshot.
  - Never re-stat afterwards: a second read races the owner's write.
  - A missing, unreadable or unparseable lock still returns null.
- `staleLockReason`:
  - Right after the read, add: `if (info?.empty) return Date.now() - info.createdAtMs > LOCK_STALE_TIMEOUT_MS ? 'malformed lock' : null;`.
  - Add a one-line why comment: acquireLock's O_EXCL create lands one syscall before its JSON write, so a young empty lock is a live owner mid-write.
  - Reuse LOCK_STALE_TIMEOUT_MS. It is already the window a live-pid lock is trusted for, so there is no new env var or doc.
  - A future mtime (clock skew) reads as young. That is the safe direction, and it matches the existing timeout check.
  - Every later check and its reason string stay unchanged.
- `acquireLock` error handling for the write:
  - After a successful openSync, wrap only the writeSync.
  - If it throws: try closeSync(fd), then try unlinkSync(lockPath), each ignoring its own error. Then logger.warn({ error }, 'Failed to write daemon lock; removed it') and return false.
  - Close before unlink: Windows keeps an open file's name until its last handle closes.
  - Why: a young empty lock now blocks every start for LOCK_STALE_TIMEOUT_MS, so our own failed write must not leave one behind.
  - The success path (closeSync, return true) and the EEXIST stale-retry loop stay unchanged. Never unlink after a successful write.
- removeStaleLock, cleanupStaleDaemonFiles, releaseLock and startDaemon stay unchanged. Their stop, status and start callers now also keep a young empty lock, which is intended.

GREEN means T1–T3 pass, and the existing 'stopDaemon refuses to signal when liveness is not tied to a healthy Moe daemon' test passes unchanged. That test removes a young non-empty 'not-json' lock.

implementationPlan.description:
ADVERSARIAL SELF-REVIEW, once, as the final step. Load adversarial-self-review.

Check:
- Two starts at the same instant: the O_EXCL create picks one owner. The other reads a young empty lock as live (T1), so at most one daemon starts.
- An owner that crashed between create and write: its empty lock is reclaimed after LOCK_STALE_TIMEOUT_MS (T2). That bounded delay is accepted.
- Clock skew: a future mtime never steals a lock. A past skew beyond the timeout falls back to today's behavior.
- Error handling on write failure: the fd is closed, the lock removed and a warn logged (T3). Nothing is unlinked after a successful write.
- A non-empty unreadable lock is still reclaimed at once.
- The diff touches only index.ts and index.test.ts, at most about 60 net lines.
- No new env var, setting or doc. No comment uses the daemonGitDocs phrases ("runs no git" and the like).

Out of scope; do not fix here. If you confirm one with a repro, file it as a separate LOW row:
- removeStaleLock's check-then-unlink TOCTOU: two contenders racing on a genuinely stale lock can delete each other's fresh lock.
- The 15s trust window for startups slower than LOCK_STALE_TIMEOUT_MS.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: A daemon.lock with no content yet is treated as a live owner while its mtime is within LOCK_STALE_TIMEOUT_MS. That is the state between acquireLock's O_EXCL create and its JSON write. staleLockReason returns null for it, so acquireLock's contender refuses and no cleanupStaleDaemonFiles caller deletes it. An empty lock older than that is still 'malformed lock' and is reclaimed. A lock write that fails after the O_EXCL create closes its fd and removes the empty lock it created, then acquireLock returns false.
acceptanceCriteria: A young empty lock: staleLockReason is null, acquireLock is false, and the lock bytes stay ''.
An empty lock whose mtime is 60s old: staleLockReason is 'malformed lock', acquireLock is true, and the lock then records this pid.
A young non-empty unparseable lock ('not-json') is still 'malformed lock'. The existing stopDaemon 'not-json' test passes unchanged.
writeSync throwing after the O_EXCL create: acquireLock is false, no daemon.lock remains, the opened fd is closed, and a following acquireLock succeeds.
invariants: The O_EXCL create stays the only way to take the lock. A young empty lock is never unlinked by a contender or by stop, status or start cleanup.
The pid-only and JSON lock paths are unchanged: the foreign, projectPath-mismatch, pid-alive and timeout checks keep their order and reason strings.
Nothing is unlinked after a successful lock write.
compatibility: Existing daemon.lock formats (pid-only digits, and JSON {pid, projectPath, createdAt}) parse exactly as before.
readLockInfo still returns null for a missing, unreadable or unparseable lock. LockInfo gains only an optional field.
No new env var or setting. MOE_LOCK_STALE_TIMEOUT_MS keeps its meaning and now also bounds the empty-lock grace.
sourceAssumptions: packages/moe-daemon/src/index.ts readLockInfo: statSync, then readFileSync(...).trim(); `if (!raw) return null`.
staleLockReason's first check returns 'malformed lock' when !info || !info.pid.
acquireLock: openSync(O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_WRONLY), then writeSync, then closeSync. On EEXIST it calls removeStaleLock and retries, up to 3 attempts.

removeStaleLock is staleLockReason's only runtime caller. It is reached from acquireLock and from cleanupStaleDaemonFiles (existingDaemonBlocksStart, startDaemon's lock wait, stopDaemon, statusDaemon).

approachesConsidered: Write to a temp file, then fs.linkSync it into place, so the lock is never empty. Rejected: hard links fail on FAT/exFAT and some network shares, so it would need a fallback path.
A bounded synchronous re-read spin on an empty lock. Rejected: the bound is arbitrary, and the spin stalls stop and status.
A new MOE_LOCK_WRITE_GRACE_MS. Rejected: it adds a knob and docs, while LOCK_STALE_TIMEOUT_MS is already the lock's trust window.
Grace for any young malformed lock. Rejected: it is not the observed window, and it changes the stopDaemon 'not-json' cleanup behavior.
Math.abs on the age. Rejected: under a future-mtime skew it would steal a fresh lock.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: daemon.lock is only a startup mutex. startDaemon acquires it before findAvailablePort and state.load, and releases it right after writeDaemonInfo. staleLockReason's only runtime caller is removeStaleLock. readLockInfo is exported for tests only. No launcher script, IDE plugin or doctor reads daemon.lock. On HEAD aeeca045 the empty branch is `if (!raw) return null;`, which staleLockReason turns into 'malformed lock'; acquireLock's EEXIST path then unlinks the owner's file and wins its retry. That is the task's repro.

- On Windows, libuv opens files with FILE_SHARE_DELETE, so an unlink of an open file leaves its name delete-pending until close. That is why close comes before unlink.
